---
title: DuckDB
---

`dazapiz.duckdb` registers Azure secrets with DuckDB's `azure` extension, so
DuckDB can query ADLS Gen2 and Blob Storage as you or as a service
principal. It needs the extra:

```sh
pip install "dazapiz[duckdb]"
```

`duckdb` is imported only when a helper runs; `import dazapiz` never needs
it. Each helper takes a connection and runs `INSTALL azure; LOAD azure`
first if the extension is not loaded yet.

## Your `az login` in DuckDB

DuckDB's own `credential_chain` cannot use the refresh token your
`az login` left behind. `set_credential_secret()` can, through any
`TokenCredential`: it asks the credential for a storage token and registers
it.

```python
import duckdb
from dazapiz import RefreshTokenCredential, refresh_token_from_az_cli
from dazapiz.duckdb import set_credential_secret

conn = duckdb.connect()
expires_on = set_credential_secret(conn, RefreshTokenCredential(refresh_token_from_az_cli()))

conn.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM 'abfss://data@myaccount.dfs.core.windows.net/sales/*.parquet'")
```

The token expires, typically after an hour, and is not refreshed in the
background. The function returns its `expires_on` (seconds since the
epoch); call it again before then to replace the secret. Keep the
`RefreshTokenCredential` and pass the same one each time: it keeps the
access token in memory until five minutes before expiry.

Any other credential works the same way, such as
`azure.identity.DefaultAzureCredential()`.

## The other secrets

| Function | DuckDB provider | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_credential_secret(conn, credential)` | `access_token` | a token from any `TokenCredential` |
| `set_token_secret(conn, token)` | `access_token` | an access token you already have |
| `set_sp_secret(conn, tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)` | `service_principal` | DuckDB redeems the secret itself |
| `set_chain_secret(conn, chain="default")` | `credential_chain` | DuckDB finds a credential itself (`"cli"`, `["managed_identity", "env"]`, ...) |

`list_secrets(conn)` shows the registered Azure secrets (DuckDB redacts
their values) and `azure_settings(conn)` the Azure settings, both as DuckDB
relations: `.fetchall()`, `.df()` or print them.

The functions are ports of `quak`'s `az_set_*_secret()`, `az_list_secrets()`,
`az_conn_settings()` and `az_tune()`, and run the same SQL.

## One secret per account

Without `account`, the secret is named `dazapiz_default` and applies to every
Azure URL. With `account`, it is named `dazapiz_<account>` and scoped to that
account's hosts, so different accounts can use different credentials:

```python
set_credential_secret(conn, mine)                           # dazapiz_default
set_sp_secret(conn, tenant, client_id, secret, account="shared")  # dazapiz_shared
```

The scope covers `abfss://` and `abfs://` on `<account>.dfs.core.windows.net`
and `az://` and `azure://` on `<account>.blob.core.windows.net`; a name with
a dot is taken as the host itself. DuckDB picks the secret whose scope is
the longest prefix of the URL.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Delta tables need an unscoped secret

Delta tables never match an account-scoped secret. Register an unscoped
one (no `account`) for Delta tables; scoped secrets work for Parquet, CSV
and JSON.
:::

`dazapiz_*` names never collide with `quak`'s `quak_*` secrets in a shared
DuckDB file.

## Tuning reads

`tune()` sets the Azure transfer settings; arguments left `None` are left
alone:

```python
from dazapiz.duckdb import tune

tune(conn, concurrency=8, chunk_size=1_048_576, buffer_size=8_388_608)
```

| Argument | DuckDB setting |
| --- | --- |
| `concurrency` | `azure_read_transfer_concurrency` |
| `chunk_size` | `azure_read_transfer_chunk_size` (bytes) |
| `buffer_size` | `azure_read_buffer_size` (bytes) |
| `transport` | `azure_transport_option_type` (`"default"`, `"curl"`) |
| `metadata_cache` | `enable_http_metadata_cache` |
| `context_cache` | `azure_context_caching` |

It warns when the buffer size is not a multiple of the chunk size.
